eligibility_note: Own PLS estimation, ICT (mobile, internet, broadband) exposure, 86 economies, Gini outcome (family 4). Weakly eligible: ICT is linked to Gini only indirectly via gender inequality, and the income-group moderation concerns the gender-Gini link, not ICT.

sample_corrections.n_economies: 86 in abstract and data section; Limitations say 'we limited the number of countries in our research to 85' (p.722) - record already flags this

results.correction: Values and p-values match Table 4. Only T1 is significant at 5%; T2-T4 are at 10% only. Standardized betas, not elasticities.
Matches Table 2 and Table 5 (ICT-GII rows). This is ICT to gender inequality, not to Gini, so it is not a family 4 outcome of ICT. T2-T4 p>0.05.
Matches Table 2. Exposure is gender inequality, not ICT, so it should not count as an ICT effect on Gini.

heterogeneity.correction: Interaction values and p-values match Table 5. Moderator is development status (larger value for developed, lower for developing), no threshold given. Moderates the gender-Gini path, not the ICT effect.
heterogeneity.quote: Development status (T3) * Gender inequality (T3) -> Income inequality (T3) 0.076 0.008

income_group_note: No separate group estimates; only a developed/developing moderator on the gender-Gini path. Record says 'not reported' for each group, which is correct.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - causal language and policy advice with no strategy for reverse causation.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - composite of mobile, internet, broadband is reasonable adoption proxy; the authors concede it does not capture all ICT dimensions.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: too_harsh - 86 countries is a decent cross-section and the four-year window is short but not a selection problem; moderate fits better, though the 85/86 inconsistency is minor.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - World Bank Gini and UNDP GII are standard but sparse across countries.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - separate per-year standardized paths, ICT absent from the Gini equation, and a T1 versus T2-T4 gap in magnitude make estimates hard to interpret.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - p of 0.054-0.099 described as significant.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious overall is fair: causal framing, no identification, and only indirect ICT-Gini evidence.

problems: No invented numbers found. All table values match the text. Result 3 (and result 2, which is labelled family 4) are not ICT effects on Gini; only result 1 is an ICT-Gini estimate and it is an indirect mediation effect.
